---
title: "Martinec et al. (2018)"
---

> Martinec, Z., Klemann, V., van der Wal, W., Riva, R. E. M., Spada, G., Sun,
> Y., Melini, D., Kachuck, S. B., Barletta, V., Simon, K., A, G. and James,
> T. S. (2018). A benchmark study of numerical implementations of the sea
> level equation in GIA modelling. *Geophysical Journal International* 215(1),
> 389-414. doi:[10.1093/gji/ggy280](https://doi.org/10.1093/gji/ggy280)

The licence of the paper is recorded on [its protocol page](../protocol/martinec2018.qmd).

Ten codes, five cases of increasing complexity, all on the same incompressible
earth model as Spada et al. (2011) and all using the same spherical cap of
angular radius 10 degrees, moved and rescaled. The sea level equation has no
analytic solution, so accuracy is measured as the difference from a chosen
reference, the VEGA solution of Martinec.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
from gia_mip import cases
rows = ["| Case | Title | SLE | Ice | Time | Basin | Terminal |",
        "| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | ---: |"]
for c in cases.cases("martinec2018"):
    s = c["specification"]
    rows.append(f"| [{c['published_name']}](../results/index.qmd#{c['id']}) | "
                f"{c['title']} | {s['sea_level_equation']} | {s['ice_height_model']} | "
                f"{s['time_scenario']} | {s['ocean_basin']} | {s['terminal_time_kyr']} kyr |")
Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

Case A does not solve the sea level equation and coincides with Spada et al.
(2011) test 1/2 for the cap load, which is what makes it the entry point.

## What we hold

Martinec's archives for all five cases, `resultsA_2026.zip` to
`resultsE_2026.zip`, with every contributor's curves, the VEGA reference and
the scripts that drew the published figures, and Kachuck's giapy submission.
Earlier rounds from Martinec are withdrawn. The converted data are
in `data/converted/martinec2018/`; see [the column layouts](../reference/column-layouts.qmd).

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
from gia_mip import cases
rows = ["| Case | Archive | Contributors in the paper | Reference solution |",
        "| --- | --- | ---: | --- |"]
for c in cases.cases("martinec2018"):
    r = c["reference_data"]
    rows.append(f"| {c['published_name']} | "
                f"{'`' + r['archive'] + '`' if r.get('archive') else 'not held'} | "
                f"{len(r['contributors'])} | "
                f"{r.get('reference', 'held')} |")
Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

## Two things to know before reading the data

**The files use internal case codes.** Cases B, C, D and E are `C2`, `D3`,
`E2` and `F1` inside the files. B is certain, because two of Kachuck's `C2`
files are byte-identical to files in `resultsB_2026.zip`. C and D are certain,
because Martinec's `resultsC_2026.zip` and `resultsD_2026.zip` hold only `D3`
and `E2` files and their cross-section scripts are titled "Benchmark C" and
"Benchmark D". E rests on `resultsE_2026.zip`, which holds only `F1` files
and compares the ocean area and h_UF, as the paper does for case E.

**Benchmark A's VEGA file is not the published reference.** `Z_ZM_load.out`
is a second VEGA run. The published reference is recoverable: every
`Z_<code>_load_diff.out` is that contributor minus VEGA, so adding a
contributor's profile back onto its own difference file returns it. Five
contributors agree to better than one millimetre across the whole range.
See [the corrections](../data/corrections.qmd).
